findings.title: The pre-namespace key migration needed room for the library twice and threw on a full quota
findings.impact: A browser whose local library is large — the founder's account holds the whole catalogue — got a blank page and nothing else. ensureProfiles() is the first statement of App.init(), so QuotaExceededError killed the boot before the router ran: every asset returned 200, the server log was clean, and the site was unusable with no way to tell why.
findings.suggestedFix: Rename the key by freeing the old value before writing the new one, and put it back if the write still fails, so the migration can never stop the application starting.

findings.title: 11 703 anime carry no anilist_id, so the AniList enricher can never match them
findings.impact: 13 038 of 32 390 titles have no description. 11 703 of those are unreachable by design rather than by accident: upsertMedia() finds its row with SELECT ... WHERE anilist_id = $1 and returns false when there is none, and those rows were seeded from a MAL-keyed dump holding mal_id only. No number of enrichment runs will ever fill them, so a third of the catalogue shows an empty synopsis for ever.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: linkAniListIdsFromMal() looks the AniList id up by MAL id, 50 at a time, and the basic pass runs it first — so a row seeded with only a mal_id becomes reachable instead of being skipped for ever. Ids AniList does not know are recorded as not_found rather than retried.

findings.title: The SPA fallback answers a missing client module with index.html and a 200
findings.impact: Any import that stops resolving — a file moved by a restructure, a typo in a path — is served as HTML with status 200 instead of 404. The browser refuses to run it as a module and the page goes blank, while every check an operator would make says the site is healthy: the JS URL returns 200, the server logs nothing. This is what made YUME-AUDIT-0001 take so long to find and it will do the same to the next one.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: the SPA fallback no longer answers for a path inside the client's own asset tree, so a missing file under /src, /css or /assets is a 404 with a problem document. Verified in a browser: /src/app/nope.js returns 404 application/problem+json, and /admin/audit still returns the application.

findings.title: POST /v1/anime/resolve lets any signed-in account create catalogue rows at the global rate limit
findings.impact: The route creates an anime stub for an AniList id it has not seen, and carries only the 300-requests-a-minute global limit — no WRITE_LIMIT and no per-account cap. One ordinary account can insert hundreds of thousands of rows a day into the anime table, which is the table this instance most needs to protect, and every one of them appears in search and in the sitemap.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: WRITE_LIMIT on the route, a 200-a-day per-account cap on new catalogue rows (ANIME_STUB_DAILY_MAX), and an anime.create audit entry that records who added each one — which is also what the cap counts. Verified: the 201st creation answers 429 and an existing title still resolves.

findings.title: docker build -t yume-test . fails: the restructure left no Dockerfile at the repository root
findings.impact: The documented and habitual build command exits with "failed to read dockerfile: open Dockerfile: no such file or directory". CI passes because .github/workflows/check.yml names the file explicitly, so anyone building by hand — which is how a release gets made in a hurry — hits a failure CI cannot warn them about.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: the Dockerfile is at the repository root, where `docker build .` looks for it. docker-compose.yml, the CI workflow, README and paths.test.ts all follow it. `docker build -t yume-test .` exits 0.

findings.title: Access and refresh tokens live in localStorage, where script can read them
findings.impact: There is no cookie anywhere in the API, so HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite are not merely unset — they are unavailable. Any script that runs on the origin can read a refresh token good for 30 days and use it from anywhere. The strict CSP (script-src 'self') is the only thing standing in front of it, which makes one injection into a same-origin file a full account takeover rather than a session-long nuisance.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: the refresh token is an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to /v1/auth, and the client drops the field on the way in. Verified in a browser: localStorage holds accessToken and expiresAt only. The access token stays there deliberately — fifteen minutes, and user() is read synchronously before anything is fetched. A client loaded before the change still refreshes from the body, so a deploy signs nobody out.

findings.title: The donut legend interpolates its label into innerHTML without escaping
findings.impact: Charts.donut() builds each legend row as an HTML string containing d.label and d.color. Today those are genre and format names from the catalogue, so exploiting it needs the anime.edit permission — but it is an unescaped HTML sink on a page an administrator opens, which makes it a privilege-escalation step rather than a harmless one, and nothing stops a future caller passing a username.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: the legend row is built from elements and textContent, and the swatch colour goes through the style property. A regression test feeds it an img/onerror payload and asserts it comes back as text.

findings.title: The metric-age probe sequentially scans every system_metrics partition
findings.impact: SELECT max(created_at) FROM system_metrics has no index it can use — the only index is (metric, created_at DESC) — so the diagnostics page reads all three partitions in full. Measured on the live database: a parallel sequential scan over 231 944 rows, 2 689 buffers, 28 ms, and it grows with the retention window. pg_stat_user_tables records 34 198 sequential scans of the current partition.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: 0039 indexes created_at on the partitioned parent and the probe asks only about the last seven days, so the planner prunes and walks one index backwards. Measured on 200 000 rows: index-only scans, 8 buffers, 0.21 ms, against 2 689 buffers and 28 ms before.

findings.title: Withdrawn: the mapping-conflict review queue already exists
findings.impact: This finding was wrong. GET /v1/admin/catalogue/metadata/conflicts and POST .../conflicts/:id/resolve have existed since the conflicts table did, and the admin Metadata section lists every unresolved pair with both titles, a seen count and a Mark reviewed button. It was asserted from the migration comment without grepping for a reader, which is the mistake the audit brief warned against. Nothing is wrong and nothing was changed.
findings.suggestedFix: No action. The queue is at Admin → Metadata → Unresolved id collisions.

findings.title: 1 335 anime have an AniList id and still no synopsis after enrichment
findings.impact: These are the rows the enricher can reach and did not fill. Whether that is AniList genuinely having no description, a run that has not covered them yet, or resolveFields refusing the write cannot be told apart from the outside, because metadata_runs records counts and not per-row outcomes. For a viewer it is an anime page with an empty description and no explanation.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: 0040 adds metadata_attempts, one row per title per source, and the enricher records what resolveFields decided — updated, unchanged, no_synopsis, not_found, locked or failed. The Metadata section shows the split, so "AniList has no description" stops looking like "nobody has tried".

findings.title: Several user-facing write routes carry only the global rate limit
findings.impact: WRITE_LIMIT is applied to eight routes; these are not among them, and 300 requests a minute is a flooding budget rather than a limit: POST /v1/comments/:id/like, PATCH /v1/forum/topics/:id, PUT and DELETE /v1/me/library/:animeId, DELETE /v1/me/favorites/:animeId, PATCH /v1/me/progress/:episodeId, PATCH /v1/profiles/me, PATCH and DELETE /v1/me/settings, POST and DELETE /v1/w2g. Vote manipulation and write amplification against the database are both cheap.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: WRITE_LIMIT is on all eleven. Verified: PATCH /v1/profiles/me now answers with x-ratelimit-limit: 30 rather than 300.

findings.title: 222 canonical titles are held by more than one anime row
findings.impact: Duplicate catalogue entries split a show's episodes, its library entries and its comments across two ids, and the viewer sees the same title twice in search with different progress on each. Some are legitimate — AniList splits seasons that MyAnimeList keeps together — which is exactly why they need looking at rather than assuming.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: findDuplicates gained an exact-title pass that does not require the year and format to agree, and it is the default. Against the live catalogue it proposes 246 pairs where the old scan saw 48, in 73 ms. The similar-title pass is unchanged and now opt-in — see YUME-AUDIT-0023.

findings.title: The name /v1/admin/audit is already taken by the audit trail
findings.impact: The audit-status report was specified to live at GET /v1/admin/audit, which is the audit log's route. Fastify refuses a duplicate route at startup, so registering the second one would have stopped the whole application from booting rather than failing at the request. The report is served from /v1/admin/audit/report instead, and the admin section key audit-log was freed so that /admin/audit could name the new page.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the two audits distinguishable by name — audit log and audit report — everywhere they are referred to.

findings.title: The palette has no yellow, so two severity levels share the amber hue
findings.impact: Severity is meant to read critical red, high orange, medium yellow, low grey. The tokens offer red, amber and grey and nothing between amber and green, so high and medium are separated by lightness within one hue rather than by hue. The badges carry the word as well as the colour so nothing is conveyed by colour alone, but at badge size the two amber steps are harder to tell apart than the design intends.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: --yellow-400/500 added, and the four severities are now four hues. Measured in a browser: rgb(236,101,101), rgb(248,195,89), rgb(251,232,106), rgb(128,128,128). They point at the 400 steps, which the light theme redefines darker.

findings.title: Release entries are inserted one statement at a time
findings.impact: writeEntries() issues one INSERT per line of a release. It is inside a transaction and a release has a handful of lines, so the cost is small — but it is a round trip per row on a request path, and the shape scales with whatever somebody pastes in.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: one INSERT ... SELECT FROM unnest(...) WITH ORDINALITY, which also keeps the order the lines arrived in.

findings.title: Achievement grants run two statements per achievement earned
findings.impact: grantNew() loops over the newly earned achievements with an INSERT and then an XP insert inside the loop. Only newly earned ones are in the list, so this is normally zero or one iteration — but a founder import that crosses every threshold at once makes it the whole catalogue in one request.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: one INSERT for the whole set and one for the XP events, with RETURNING deciding which grants were this call's — so the concurrent-grant rule is enforced by the database rather than by reading back.

findings.title: 512 anime hold no episode rows at all
findings.impact: The anime page offers no episode list and the watch route has nothing to open. Some are legitimately unreleased, so this is a number to look at rather than a fault on its own — it is listed because nothing currently reports it.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: coverage() counts it and the Metadata section shows it beside the other three gap figures.

findings.title: Some controls are under 32 px tall at 375 px wide
findings.impact: Measured in a real browser at 375x812: the library tabs are 30 px tall, the admin range buttons 24 px, and the footer links 16 to 21 px. All clear the 24x24 WCAG 2.5.8 minimum except the footer links, and all are below the 44 px that thumbs actually want. Nothing is unreachable; several things are fiddly.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: tabs, range buttons, small buttons, dashboard widget links, footer navigation, genre chips and the spotlight credit all clear 40-44 px at 375. Verified in a browser: nothing under 32 px remains on home, list, profile or dashboard, except the three attribution links inside a running sentence in the footer, which sit at 27 px — above WCAG 2.5.8's 24 px, and a 44 px box there would break the line rather than enlarge the target.

findings.title: POST /v1/auth/logout and /logout-all accept a body with no schema
findings.impact: They are the only two write routes in the API whose body is read without a JSON schema. Both coerce safely — (request.body ?? {}) and a hash of whatever refreshToken holds — so there is nothing exploitable here today; it is the one gap in otherwise complete validation coverage.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: both take a body schema with additionalProperties false.

findings.title: Withdrawn: the extension permissions were already removed
findings.impact: This finding was wrong. Migration 0031 deleted the extension_* permission rows and their grants, sparing theme.publish; nothing matching extension% is left in the table. What remains is the deliberate `planned` catalogue — 326 rows across ai, streaming, gamification and the rest — which is a labelled roadmap rather than a claim that they are enforced, and the honest opposite of the defect this described.
findings.suggestedFix: No action. The `planned` status is what stops those rows claiming to be enforced.

findings.title: Investigated: anime_relations is read through an index, not scanned
findings.impact: Measured rather than left open. The relations lookup on the anime detail path is an index-only scan of anime_relations_pkey — 59 rows, 0.87 ms. The correlated NOT EXISTS in the duplicate scan, the other reader, resolves to a BitmapOr over the same index. The sequential-scan counter is historical and averages 447 rows a scan against a 22 602-row table, which is small correlated probes rather than full reads. No index is missing.
findings.suggestedFix: No action. The planner was right; the counter was the wrong thing to read it by.

findings.title: One web test cannot run without the workspace being installed
findings.impact: test/achievements.test.mjs reaches into apps/api and fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package '@yume/database' on a checkout where npm ci has not been run. The other 22 files in the suite do not, so the failure looks like a broken test rather than a missing install.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed: the catalogue and evaluate() moved to achievement-catalogue.ts, which imports nothing. achievements.ts re-exports them, so no caller changed, and the test compares two arrays without a database client.

findings.title: The similar-title duplicate scan takes 68 seconds on this catalogue
findings.impact: Found while fixing YUME-AUDIT-0012, and it is why nobody had worked through the duplicates: opening the tab ran this. similarity() is a function call, so the trigram index cannot serve it, and every pair inside every (year, format) bucket is compared — 68 seconds measured on the live catalogue, against 73 ms for the exact-title pass. The operator now gets the fast pass by default and presses a button for this one, so nothing is blocked; the scan itself is still unusable for a catalogue this size.
findings.suggestedFix: Bound the comparison differently — a precomputed normalised-title key, or a periodic offline pass writing candidates to a table — rather than a self-join. A LATERAL rewrite against the GIN index was measured at 165 seconds and is not the answer.
